rules.covers: Account deletion: the DELETE endpoint always calls the erasure function. Checks the call only, not what the function deletes.

ask_parts_not_covered.part: When a user deletes their account, their data is deleted everywhere (all tables holding user data)
Customer data is not kept longer than 2 years

assumptions: 'Their stuff everywhere' means every table with a user link (user_id, customer_id, requester_email), not only the users table.
The only DELETE endpoint in the workspace is DELETE /account; verbs scope therefore covers the deletion path.
The customer wants an advisory policy first, not blocking, since the template and brief default to advisory.
2 years is a retention limit on personal data; the customer has not said which tables or what counts as the start of the period.
orders and audit_log may need to be kept for legal reasons; I did not decide that and did not write a rule for it.
confusions: object.statement_required says it requires a call to a function, but nothing in the catalogue says whether a required function must itself delete particular tables; a policy that says 'deletes everywhere' has no check to express it.
table.coverage_required (RET-002) confirms a cleanup task exists for each tagged table, not that it deletes the right rows; the 2-year cutoff (a created_at filter) cannot be checked.

Whether a 'retained' tag must be added to tables before RET-002 can run is clear from the template's 'needs: tags', but the skill's rule 6 (propose the tag separately) and the template's example (tags: [retained]) do not say what to do when no table carries the tag: whether to write the rule anyway or stop.
The catalogue's object.statement_required description does not say whether 'placement: unconditional' means the call must be in the endpoint's own stack or may be in a called function.
The parser warned that verbs only matches endpoints and suggested object_kinds; the skill does not mention that verbs need object_kinds to be explicit for a clean parse.
No recipe or template exists for 'deletion reaches every personal-data table'; the catalogue only has the RET-002 and RET-001 templates, which cover related but different things.
wished_for: A check that verifies a delete function removes or clears every table with a link to the deleted entity (for example, every table with user_id -> users), or a way to name the expected tables.
A template for GDPR erasure (Article 17) and a template for retention periods (Article 5(1)(e)) that takes a retention period, not just a cleanup task.
A check that tests a timestamp filter on cleanup tasks (for example, created_at older than N days).
Example of how to propose a tag on tables for the customer to decide, and a way to show which tables would be tagged before any change is made.
A recipe that combines object.statement_required with table references, for a 'deletion path covers these tables' check.
parse_errors_seen: Rule warning: verbs only matches endpoints, so this rule inspects endpoints only; set object_kinds: ["query"] to say so. (resolved by adding object_kinds)
why_confidence: The policy parses and checks that the DELETE endpoint calls delete_user_account, which is a real but narrow part of the ask. It does not check that deletion covers all tables with user data (orders, support_tickets and audit_log are not deleted by the current function), and it does not enforce the 2-year retention limit, which needs a retained tag on tables that the workspace lacks. I did not run xano policy evaluate, so no finding is confirmed.
